profiles.bio: CS student at Stanford focusing on accessible web architecture and responsive systems.
Lead Technical Mentor & Staff Engineer. Reviewing student evidence for correctness and accessibility.

challenges.title: Responsive Login Page
challenges.description: Build a production-ready, accessible login interface with client-side validation, accessible form controls, loading state, and fluid responsive styling across mobile and desktop viewports.
requirements: Semantic <form> with explicitly associated <label> elements for email and password fields.
Input validation checking valid email format and password minimum length (8 characters).
Descriptive inline error messages linked to inputs via aria-describedby when invalid.
Responsive centered card container that adapts gracefully below 640px width without horizontal scroll.
Interactive submit button with clear hover, focus-visible outline, and disabled/loading state.
acceptance_criteria: All inputs use appropriate type attributes ("email", "password").
Form submission is intercepted with preventDefault and triggers field-level validation.
Errors clear appropriately when user types valid input.
Mobile viewport tested to prevent overflowing inputs or clipped padding.

challenges.title: Interactive Task Manager
challenges.description: Implement a complete interactive task manager that handles task addition, completion toggling, deletion, filtering (All, Active, Completed), duplicate prevention, and persistent browser storage.
requirements: Text input to add tasks, rejecting empty strings and whitespace-only submissions.
Checkboxes or toggle buttons to mark items completed with visual strike-through / dimming.
Delete action per task with keyboard accessibility.
Live task counter displaying active remaining items.
Filter tabs: "All", "Active", and "Completed" with clean client-side state filtering.
LocalStorage persistence so state is restored on page reload.
Duplicate task prevention with friendly warning feedback.
acceptance_criteria: Pressing Enter in the input adds the task immediately.
Tasks cannot be added with duplicate titles (case-insensitive trim check).
Filter buttons update view instantaneously without page reloading.
Deleting all items leaves an informative, clean empty state.

criteria.name: Required Functionality & State Management
criteria.description: Adding, completing, deleting tasks, filter tabs, and persistence to localStorage.

criteria.name: Code Correctness & Architecture
criteria.description: Immutable state updates, safe JSON parsing, decoupled DOM rendering, and clean lifecycle.

criteria.name: UI & Responsive Interaction
criteria.description: Intuitive micro-interactions, empty states, task counters, and keyboard accessibility (Enter/Esc).

criteria.name: Input Validation & Edge Cases
criteria.description: Whitespace sanitization, duplicate title rejection, boundary limits, and long string handling.

criteria.name: Readability & Maintainability
criteria.description: Predictable variable naming, typed interfaces, descriptive comments, and modular structure.

challenges.title: Debug the Broken Webpage
challenges.description: Diagnose and fix 4 critical intentional bugs across HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and security/sanitization in a broken shopping cart preview, providing a detailed root-cause explanation for each fix.
requirements: Bug 1: Fix form submit loop caused by missing preventDefault or button attributes.
Bug 2: Fix unhandled Promise rejection and asynchronous rendering race condition in data fetching.
Bug 3: Fix CSS flex layout break causing horizontal viewport blowout on mobile screens (< 480px).
Bug 4: Fix XSS vulnerability where user review comments are injected with unescaped innerHTML.
Provide a clear, written 4-part explanation detailing what caused each bug and how your solution fixes it.
acceptance_criteria: Submitting checkout does not trigger full page refresh.
Item quantities recalculate total correctly using Number coercion to avoid string concatenation.
No text or card spills over screen boundary on mobile width.
User-provided string comments are rendered safely using textContent or safe DOM nodes.
Written explanations accurately identify the root causes.

criteria.name: Accuracy of Bug Fixes
criteria.description: Correctly addresses all 4 bugs: form reload, async data race & coercion, layout overflow, and XSS injection.

criteria.name: Root Cause Analysis & Explanation
criteria.description: Depth, technical precision, and clarity of the written explanation for each defect.

criteria.name: Security & Defensive Coding
criteria.description: Proper sanitization (textContent / text nodes) and safe async handling (Promise.all).

criteria.name: Prevention of Regressions
criteria.description: Clean integration without introducing secondary styling or functional flaws.

challenges.title: REST API Data Fetcher & Cache
challenges.description: Build an async data fetcher component featuring loading skeletons, exponential retry logic, client-side memory caching, search filtering, and robust HTTP error boundaries.
requirements: Async fetch with AbortController for request cancellation on unmount/search change.
In-memory cache with TTL (Time-To-Live) to avoid redundant network round-trips.
Graceful loading state with visual skeleton placeholder.
Explanatory error state with an interactive "Retry" button.
Debounced search input (300ms) to filter returned items by name/tag.
acceptance_criteria: Rapid typing in search cancels previous in-flight requests.
Cached requests return instantly without showing full loading skeleton.
Network failures (e.g. 500 status) display friendly user explanation and retry capability.

criteria.name: Async Data Flow & Error Handling
criteria.description: Proper try/catch, HTTP status checking, retry mechanism, and AbortController cancellation.

criteria.name: Performance & Caching Strategy
criteria.description: Accurate TTL expiration check, memory leak avoidance, and instant cache hit return.

criteria.name: UI States & Accessibility
criteria.description: Distinct loading, error, empty, and populated states with visible focus and aria-live announcements.

criteria.name: TypeScript & Code Architecture
criteria.description: Strict type safety, generic parameters, and decoupled testable methods.

submissions.explanation: Comprehensive semantic login page with full ARIA live error association, blur validation, responsive grid viewport, and WCAG AA focus rings.

criteria.name: Required Functionality & State Management
criteria.evidence: Implemented basic task push, toggle, deletion, and stored to localStorage: `taskList.push(...)` and `localStorage.setItem(...)`.
criteria.feedback: Task addition and deletion work, but filter tabs ("All", "Active", "Completed") and active task counter were completely omitted.

criteria.name: Code Correctness & Architecture
criteria.evidence: Global `const taskList = [];` with inline event handlers in HTML strings `onclick="toggleTask(${t.id})"`.
criteria.feedback: Avoid inline HTML string onclick handlers. Also missing safe JSON parsing on load in case localStorage contains corrupt data.

criteria.name: UI & Responsive Interaction
criteria.evidence: Basic createElement inside `render()` loop; no empty state or keyboard accessibility.
criteria.feedback: No visual distinction between empty task list and loaded items. Needs keyboard listeners (e.g. Enter to add).

criteria.name: Input Validation & Edge Cases
criteria.feedback: Only checks for empty string; fails to trim whitespace, meaning users can submit empty spaces. No duplicate task prevention.

criteria.name: Readability & Maintainability
criteria.evidence: Functions are short and understandable with self-descriptive names.
criteria.feedback: Good straightforward logic, but would benefit from encapsulating in a class or modular state store.

strengths: Successfully persists task array to browser localStorage on modification.
Clear, readable procedural functions for adding, toggling, and removing tasks.
improvements: Sanitize input using `.trim()` and prevent duplicate task entries.
Implement the required filter tabs (All, Active, Completed) and task counter.
Replace inline `onclick` string handlers with standard `addEventListener`.
limitations: Static AST and source code inspection performed; runtime DOM events simulated.

criteria.name: Required Functionality & State Management
criteria.evidence: Implemented class `TaskApp` with `addTask`, `toggleTask`, `deleteTask`, `setFilter`, `getFilteredTasks()`, and dynamic active item counter.
criteria.feedback: All core features implemented with fidelity. Clean filter tabs and reactive active item counter.

criteria.name: Code Correctness & Architecture
criteria.evidence: Safe loading with try/catch fallback in `loadSafe()`: `try { return data ? JSON.parse(data) : []; } catch (e) { ... }`
criteria.feedback: Excellent error handling on JSON parsing and modular event listeners attached via `addEventListener`.

criteria.name: UI & Responsive Interaction
criteria.evidence: Dynamic empty state (`No tasks yet. Add one above!`), Enter key binding in `bindEvents()`, and `aria-label` on delete buttons.
criteria.feedback: High accessibility discipline with explicit labels and empty states. Could add smooth exit animation on delete.

criteria.name: Input Validation & Edge Cases
criteria.evidence: `const title = rawTitle.trim(); if (!title) ...` and case-insensitive duplicate check: `this.tasks.some(t => t.title.toLowerCase() === title.toLowerCase())`.
criteria.feedback: Robust edge-case handling with clear visual error messaging rendered via `showError`.

criteria.name: Readability & Maintainability
criteria.evidence: Well-structured ES6 class with separation between state storage, validation, rendering, and DOM event binding.
criteria.feedback: Highly maintainable, readable code following modern frontend development best practices.

strengths: Comprehensive resolution of Attempt 1 weaknesses: added duplicate checking, whitespace trimming, and filter tabs.
Defensive programming with `try/catch` wrapped localStorage access preventing corrupt data crashes.
Accessible DOM output including `aria-label` for delete buttons and `select-none` on checkboxes.
improvements: Consider adding an edit task in-place feature for advanced interaction.
Could abstract DOM rendering to a template helper or lightweight component pattern.
limitations: Static evaluation conducted on provided JavaScript source code.

criteria.name: Required Functionality & Form Handling
criteria.evidence: `form.addEventListener("submit", (e) => { e.preventDefault(); ... })`, regex format test, length check.
criteria.feedback: Complete form interception, custom email regex validation, password length constraint.

criteria.name: Semantic HTML & Accessibility
criteria.feedback: Outstanding accessibility implementation with ARIA attributes and visible focus indicators.

criteria.name: UI & Responsive Layout
criteria.evidence: `body { display: grid; place-items: center; padding: 16px; }` and `.card { width: 100%; max-width: 420px; }`.
criteria.feedback: Fluid grid centering that handles small mobile screens naturally without horizontal scrolling.

criteria.name: Input Validation & Edge Cases
criteria.evidence: Blur event validation on email and password inputs with trim sanitization.
criteria.feedback: Instant blur feedback allows users to correct mistakes before submitting.

criteria.name: Code Cleanliness & Maintainability
criteria.evidence: CSS variables used for palette, semantic markup, concise JavaScript functions.
criteria.feedback: Very clean vanilla code structure with clear intent and zero external bloat.

strengths: Fluid mobile-first card layout that scales seamlessly without breaking viewport bounds.
improvements: Add a "show/hide password" toggle for enhanced mobile usability.
Add visual loading spinner to submit button during submission.
limitations: Static DOM and CSS rule inspection; responsive behavior verified via viewport CSS metrics.

mentor_reviews.mentor_title: Lead Technical Mentor, Stanford Web Systems Lab
mentor_reviews.feedback: Verified clean, production-grade responsive form implementation. Tested accessibility attributes with NVDA screen reader conventions: proper aria-live and role="alert" alerts fire predictably on blur, and mobile viewport scales down to 320px without layout distortion.
